question: Is Whataburger Only in Texas?
quick_answer: No. Whataburger is most famous in Texas and the brand is deeply tied to the state, but it is not Texas-only. It has hundreds of locations across the southern US and has been expanding into new states in recent years, moving well beyond its original footprint.

body.heading: Whataburger is a Texas icon, but not Texas-only
body.text: Whataburger is strongly associated with Texas, where it was founded in 1950 and where most people first encounter it. But it has long operated across the broader South, and today it has hundreds of restaurants outside Texas, so being 'a Texas thing' is more about its identity than its actual map.

body.heading: Where you can find Whataburger
body.text: Beyond Texas, Whataburger has a big presence across the southern US, including states like Florida, Arizona, Georgia, Alabama, Louisiana and the Carolinas. It has traditionally been a Sun Belt chain, strongest in the South and Southwest.

body.heading: The recent expansion
body.text: After the 2019 majority-stake sale to an investment firm, Whataburger has been expanding into new markets it never served before, such as Tennessee, Kansas and Colorado. So the chain is steadily moving north and out of its original base, and more states are getting their first Whataburgers.

faqs.a: No. Whataburger started in Texas and is strongest there, but it operates hundreds of restaurants across the southern US and is expanding into new states.
Besides Texas, Whataburger is found across much of the South and Southwest, including Florida, Arizona, Georgia, Alabama, Louisiana and the Carolinas, with newer markets being added.

faqs.q: Why do people think Whataburger is only in Texas?
faqs.a: Because it was founded there, is headquartered there and is a cultural icon in Texas. Its identity is so tied to the state that many assume it never left.
